title: 🚀 The US Space Force accelerates its orbital data network.. regional coverage this year and global in 2027!
body: 🚀 The US Space Force accelerates its orbital data network.. regional coverage this year and global in 2027!

The US Department of the Air Force has announced it is speeding up the building of the Space Data Network, a government-owned satellite constellation to move data quickly and securely around the world for joint forces and their allies. The announcement came on 21 November, after three successful launches within two weeks, a pace that reflects how fast the programme is moving.

The network will work as an interlinked web in orbit, connecting US command-and-control systems and allied forces with constant, seamless contact, without relying on commercial networks. The announced timeline is ambitious: regional capability before the end of 2026, and global support in 2027. The latest of the three launches was a secret mission that lifted off on 20 November from Vandenberg Base in California, with an undisclosed payload, and its rocket returned to Earth minutes after launch.

The stated goal is secure, fast communication carrying data between sensors and defence systems, at a time when major powers are racing over space infrastructure. Although the details of the satellites themselves are secret, the launch pace — three missions in two weeks — shows the constellation is growing fast, and that 2027 will be its real year of testing.
Simply put: a military internet in space, government-owned and covering the world in 2027 — will satellites become the next great arena of competition?
